name: ai-gateway.setpoint-read
purpose: Read every row of ai-gateway's improve setpoint in one submission from the seven route measures and the evidence sample, and report each as in band, out of band, or unavailable.

window_token.description: measures TimeWindow token; each measure binding takes window={"token": <this>}.

evidence_sample.description: Most recent route evidence rows behind local-share; the binding returns at most 50.

assumptions: ai-gateway is running and its measures and routing bindings are reachable from the kernel
measures bindings accept window as a TimeWindow message {token}; a bare string such as last_7d fails to encode
protojson omits zero-valued fields, so a missing count on breaker-open or capacity-rejections is a real zero when total is above zero
local-share is read from the most recent evidence rows, not from a window; the reading states its basis
each call runs in its own program-runtime session; session variables persist across submissions
the caller treats an unavailable row as unknown, never as zero

protojson omits zero-valued scalars: when `total` reports routes in the window, an absent `rate` on success-rate, fallback-rate, or failure-rate is read as 0.0, exactly as absent counts are read as 0; with zero routes a rate is unavailable.
invariants: no binding with effect write or destructive is called
no row set is materialized; every reading is head(1), count, or group_by
the envelope is printed exactly once, on every path
a row with no measure behind it (cost-per-caller) is reported unavailable as pending-telemetry, never estimated from evidence rows

signals.rows: list of {row, reading, target, in_band, unavailable, reason}; one entry per setpoint row in the improve skill's table order: cost-per-caller, local-share, fallback-rate, failure-rate, breaker-open, latency-p95, capacity-rejections, success-rate, route-volume
signals.readable: count of rows read from a governed binding
signals.unavailable: count of rows not readable in-program

outputs.evidence: sensor command names, one per row
